_comment: Backgrounds (2024 Player's Handbook, chapter 4): the three abilities it raises (+2/+1 or +1/+1/+1), its origin feat (choices a background fixes, as Magic Initiate's list), two skills, a tool, and equipment (option A: items and money in copper; things the game has not got yet are paid in coin at their price) or 'gold' (option B, 50 gp). Realmwalker adds the feature, the tie to real people and places, where one starts, and the words for a life before.

acolyte.name: Acolyte
acolyte.description: You grew up in a temple: scrubbing floors, copying prayers, watching the priests take the tithes. You know the rites and the politics of your faith.

feature.name: Shelter of the Faithful
feature.text: Temples of your faith will feed and shelter you, and its priests will hear you out.

tie.text: You were raised at the temple in {place}, under the stern eye of {priest}.

personality: I quote scripture at the worst possible moments.
I see omens in everything.
I am patient with fools, which is most people.
ideal: Faith: the gods are real, and they are watching.
Charity: the hungry come first.
Power: the temple should rule, not squabbling lords.
bond: I would do anything for the old priest who raised me.
A relic was stolen from my temple, and I mean to recover it.
flaw: I judge others harshly and myself not at all.
I secretly doubt everything I preach.

artisan.name: Artisan
artisan.description: You learned a craft at someone's bench and were bound to it by indenture or by love of it. You know the price of good work, the cost of bad, and what the masters keep to themselves.

feature.name: Guild Membership
feature.text: Your guild will lodge and feed you in hard times, and speak for you before the law.

tie.text: You are a journeyman of the {guild} of {place}. Its master is {master}, who has not forgiven you for {grievance}.

personality: I believe that anything worth doing is worth doing right.
I'm rude to people who lack my commitment to hard work.
I like to talk at length about my craft.
ideal: Community: we must all do our part.
Generosity: my skills are for everyone.
Greed: I'm only in it for the money.
bond: The workshop where I learned my trade is the most important place in the world to me.
I owe my guild a great debt for forging me into who I am.
flaw: I'll do anything to get my hands on something rare or priceless.
I'm never satisfied with what I have.

charlatan.name: Charlatan
charlatan.description: You sold cures that cured nothing, relics that were last year's bones, and certainty to people who had none. You can read a mark in the time it takes them to put down their cup.

feature.name: False Identity
feature.text: You keep a second name, with papers and a story to match. Clerks, innkeepers and minor officials accept it until someone who knew the first one walks in.

tie.text: Your old partner in the trade is {contact}, who works the market in {place} and still holds half your takings. In {bounty_place} you are wanted for {crime}, and the reward is {bounty}.

personality: I have a different story for every stranger, and I like all of them.
I flatter first and ask second, and I mean neither.
I laugh loudest at my own jokes so that nobody has time to check them.
ideal: Independence: nobody owns me, and I owe nobody an honest day.
Fairness: I only take from those who can spare it.
Craft: a good lie is made as carefully as a good boot.
bond: I once cheated a man who did not deserve it, and I mean to repay him.
A rival trickster ruined my best scheme, and I have not forgiven it.
flaw: I cannot pass a gaming table or a fool with a full purse.
I have told so many lies that I am no longer sure which of my memories are mine.

criminal.name: Criminal
criminal.description: Cutpurse, burglar, smuggler or leg-breaker. You know which watchmen take bribes and which fences pay fair, and somewhere there is a price on your head.

feature.name: Criminal Contact
feature.text: You have a contact who can pass messages, fence goods and find people who don't want to be found.

tie.text: Your contact is {contact}, a fence in {place}. In {bounty_place} the watch wants you for {crime}: there is a bounty of {bounty} on your head.

personality: I always know where the exits are.
I lie out of habit, even when the truth would serve.
I count everyone's purse the moment I meet them.
ideal: Freedom: chains are for other people.
Greed: I'll do anything for enough coin.
Honour among thieves: I never rat.
bond: Someone I love is in a gaol cell because of me.
I owe money to people who break fingers.
flaw: When I see something valuable I can't think of anything else.
I turn and run when things go bad.

entertainer.name: Entertainer
entertainer.description: You have sung for your supper in more halls than you can count. You know the old songs, the dirty ones, and which to choose for a drunk lord and which for a grieving widow.

feature.name: By Popular Demand
feature.text: Inns, taverns and noble halls will give you a bed and a meal in return for an evening's work, and the crowd will remember your name for a season.

tie.text: You came up in {guild}, the troupe of {place} under {master}. You parted from them over {grievance}, and they have not forgotten it.

personality: I know a story for every occasion, and tell it whether or not it fits.
I cannot sit in a silent room without filling it.
I change my voice depending on who is listening.
ideal: Beauty: if I make something fine, the world is a little less ugly.
Freedom: the road is better than any lord's hall.
Fame: I want my name sung when I am dead.
bond: My instrument was my teacher's, and I will not part with it.
I owe the troupe that raised me a debt I have not yet paid.
flaw: I will do almost anything for applause.
I make promises easily when drunk and keep them rarely when sober.

farmer.name: Farmer
farmer.description: You worked the land, and stood up once. Perhaps it was a tax collector's thugs, or a wolf that took children, or a hard winter you carried your village through. They still tell it, and it grows.

feature.name: Rustic Hospitality
feature.text: Common folk will hide you, feed you and lie to the authorities for you, as long as you don't endanger them.

tie.text: The people of {place} still tell how you {deed}. Their headman is {headman}.

personality: I judge people by their actions, not their words.
I'm confident in my own worth, whatever my birth.
I use long words badly.
ideal: Fairness: no one is above the law, least of all lords.
Sincerity: I say what I mean.
Destiny: something is waiting for me out there.
bond: I will protect my village, whatever it costs.
A tyrant hurt my family, and they will answer for it.
flaw: I'm convinced of the importance of my destiny.
I have a weakness for drink and a loud mouth when I'm in it.

guard.name: Guard
guard.description: You stood on a wall, or at a gate, or outside a door, and watched for trouble through the long dull hours. Mostly it did not come. When it did, you were the first it met.

feature.name: Watch-Fellows
feature.text: Gate wardens, watchmen and men-at-arms treat you as one of their own. They will tell you what the watch has seen and give you a place by their fire.

tie.text: You kept watch for {lord} of {house}, at {place}. You left the gate {how}.

personality: I notice who is standing near the door.
I speak little, and what I say is usually an order.
I make jokes at the worst moments, because the silence is worse.
ideal: Order: a road without a watchman is a road for thieves.
Loyalty: I keep my word to the man who pays me.
Mercy: most of those I arrested were hungry.
bond: I let someone through a gate once, and I still wonder what became of them.
The man who relieved me on the wall is the best friend I have.
flaw: I suspect every stranger, including those who have done me no harm.
I will look the other way for a small coin and hate myself after.

guide.name: Guide
guide.description: You led travellers through the wild: over passes, across moors, through forests where the paths are made by deer. You know where the water is, and where the ground will not hold.

feature.name: Wanderer
feature.text: You remember the lie of the land, and you can find food and fresh water for yourself and a few others.

tie.text: You were born to the {clan}, who range around {place}. Their chief is {chief}.

personality: I watch over my friends as if they were a litter of newborn pups.
I'm always picking things up, fiddling with them.
I feel far more comfortable around animals than people.
ideal: Change: life is like the seasons.
Greater good: the strong should protect the weak.
Nature: towns are sick, and the wild is clean.
bond: My clan is the most important thing in my life.
I will bring terrible wrath down on those who harmed my home.
flaw: I am too enamoured of ale, wine and other intoxicants.
Violence is my answer to almost any challenge.

hermit.name: Hermit
hermit.description: You spent years alone in a cell, a cave or a hut at the edge of the wood, with only your thoughts and your god. Something you learned there drove you back among people.

feature.name: Quiet Welcome
feature.text: Shrines, chapels and holy folk will give you a bed and a bowl without asking much. People tell a stranger of the cloth things they would not tell their neighbours.

tie.text: You were given leave to live apart by the temple in {place}, whose priest {priest} brought you bread each month and asked no questions.

personality: I would rather listen than speak, and I forget how to do either in a crowd.
I talk to myself and sometimes answer.
I am unbothered by cold, hunger and the opinions of others.
ideal: Solitude: a quiet mind sees what a busy one misses.
Understanding: I mean to learn why the world is as it is.
Mercy: I have felt hunger and I will not see it in others.
bond: I left a discovery behind in my cell and I mean to go back for it.
I am looking for the one person who ever answered my letters.
flaw: I am too sure of what I saw in the long silence.
I do not know how to be kind without lecturing.

merchant.name: Merchant
merchant.description: You bought cheap and sold dear, and you know to the farthing what a thing is worth in a town and what it will fetch two valleys over. You also know the roads, and what they cost.

feature.name: Trade Credit
feature.text: Merchants and carriers will give you word of the roads and the markets, and shopkeepers in towns where your trade is known will give you a fair price and a little time to pay.

tie.text: You traded under {guild} in {place}, whose master is {master}. You left your place there over {grievance}, and your debts are still on their books.

personality: I put a price on everything, including things that were not for sale.
I shake hands warmly and check my purse afterwards.
I never sit with my back to the door of a counting-house.
ideal: Fair dealing: a bargain both sides regret is a good one.
Wealth: a man with coin has choices and a man without has orders.
Trade: roads are what bind the world, and I keep them open.
bond: A cart of mine was lost on the road, and I mean to find who took it.
My partner sleeps on my debts, and I cannot let him sink.
flaw: I cannot refuse a bargain, even a bad one.
I measure people by what they can pay, and tell them so.

noble.name: Noble
noble.description: You were born to land and a name. You have the manners, the connections and the enemies of your house, and you have never gone hungry except by choice.

feature.name: Position of Privilege
feature.text: People assume you belong wherever you go. Nobles receive you, and common folk make way.

tie.text: You are of {house}, whose seat is {place}. Its head is {head}, your {relation}.

personality: My flattery makes people feel like the most important person in the room.
I don't like to get dirty.
Despite my birth I don't place myself above others.
ideal: Responsibility: it is my duty to protect those beneath me.
Power: if I become strong I can take what I want.
Family: blood matters more than anything.
bond: My house's honour is mine to defend.
I am promised in marriage to someone I have never met.
flaw: I secretly believe everyone is beneath me.
I hide a shameful secret that could ruin my family.

sage.name: Sage
sage.description: You spent years among books: a scribe, a tutor, a student of old things. You know where to look for an answer, and how little most people know.

feature.name: Researcher
feature.text: If you don't know something, you usually know where it is written down, and who guards the book.

tie.text: Your old teacher, {master}, keeps a library in {place}. You left owing a book and an explanation.

personality: I use polysyllabic words to seem clever.
I'm used to helping out those who aren't as smart as I am.
I'm easily distracted by a promising thought.
ideal: Knowledge: the path to power is understanding.
Beauty: what is beautiful points toward what is true.
No limits: nothing should fetter possibility.
bond: I have an ancient text that holds terrible secrets.
I work to preserve a library, a university or a monastery.
flaw: I am easily distracted by the promise of information.
Unlocking an ancient mystery is worth a civilisation.

sailor.name: Sailor
sailor.description: You worked on the water: a coaster, a river barge, a fishing smack. You know knots, weather, bad food and what a drowned man looks like, and the land still feels as though it is moving.

feature.name: Ship's Passage
feature.text: You can usually get passage on a boat for the price of working it, and dock-folk and boatmen in any port will talk to you freely and tell you what is in the harbour.

tie.text: You grew up at {place}, by the water, and the people there still tell how you {deed}. Their headman is {headman}.

personality: I mutter about the weather even when we are indoors.
I make friends easily and lose them as quickly.
I swear in four languages, none of them politely.
ideal: Freedom: the sea belongs to no lord.
Crew: a ship is its people, and I do not leave them.
Courage: I have been afraid of the sea, and gone out on it anyway.
bond: My old captain went down with the ship, and I carry what he left me.
I have a debt to the man who pulled me from the water.
flaw: I spend my wages in the first tavern that will have me.
I do not trust anything I cannot see the bottom of.

scribe.name: Scribe
scribe.description: You have spent years with a pen in your hand, copying deeds and letters and other men's wisdom. You can read a page upside down across a table, and you have seen what is written in many wills.

feature.name: Skilled Hand
feature.text: Clerks, stewards and scholars treat you as one of their own. You can gain a seat in any record-room or library, and your hand on a letter makes it more likely to be believed.

tie.text: You were trained by {master} at {place}, who taught you your letters and the cost of knowing too much.

personality: I fuss over the neatness of my hand and the state of my pens.
I write down everything I see, and sometimes it is useful.
I would rather read than eat.
ideal: Truth: what is written down must be what happened.
Knowledge: no book should be burnt, whatever it says.
Order: a world with good records is a world with fewer quarrels.
bond: I copied a letter I was not meant to read, and I cannot forget it.
A book I loved was taken from the library, and I will find it.
flaw: I correct other people's grammar at the worst moments.
I would sooner forge a document than lie to a man's face.

soldier.name: Soldier
soldier.description: You carried a spear in somebody's war. You know drill, hunger, latrine trenches and what a pike line does to a charge.

feature.name: Military Rank
feature.text: Soldiers of your old lord still defer to your rank, and you can find a place at any camp or garrison.

tie.text: You served under {lord} of {house}, whose seat is {place}. You left the ranks {how}.

personality: I tell war stories whether or not anyone asked.
I keep my kit clean and my mouth shut.
I can't sleep without a blade to hand.
ideal: Duty: orders are orders.
Survival: the dead don't get paid.
Comradeship: I'd die for the people beside me, not for any lord.
bond: I still owe a debt to the sergeant who dragged me out of the mud.
Somewhere a village remembers what my company did to it.
flaw: I drink to forget, and it works less each year.
I obey anyone who shouts loudly enough.

wayfarer.name: Wayfarer
wayfarer.description: You grew up with no fixed home: sleeping in doorways, begging at fairs, running errands for anyone who paid. You know how to go unnoticed, and how a hungry belly sharpens the mind.

feature.name: Lucky Break
feature.text: Thieves, beggars and the poor of any town will hide you, feed you what they can spare, and tell you what the streets know, if they believe you are one of them.

tie.text: The one who looked after you on the road is {contact}, who keeps a place in {place}. In {bounty_place} the watch is after you for {crime}, and there is {bounty} on it.

personality: I eat fast and keep my back to a wall.
I hoard small things: a nail, a string, a crust.
I am wary of kindness, and doubly wary of free meals.
ideal: Survival: I do what I must, and ask nobody's pardon.
Community: the poor look after one another, since nobody else will.
Change: I will not die as I was born.
bond: A stranger once gave me a coat, and I have sworn to repay a stranger in kind.
I left a brother in the city and I mean to go back for him.
flaw: I take what I need without asking and call it fair.
I run when threatened, even when fighting would be wiser.

how: when your company was broken at a river crossing
honourably, with your pay and a limp
when the war ended and the pay stopped
deed: killed the wolf that took the miller's children
faced down the tax collector's men
led them through the winter the granary burned
pulled six people out of the flood
grievance: leaving before your debt was paid
